prompt: Candid documentary photo of a real serving of sate lilit as eaten at a small Balinese warung in Ubud: four or five long thin bamboo skewers each tightly wound with a rope-spiral of finely minced pork (or chicken) mixed with grated coconut, finely chopped lemongrass, shallots, garlic, coriander seeds, and kaffir lime, the meat pressed into a continuous spiral along the whole length of the skewer, with dark caramelised char along the ridges of the spiral. A small mound of sambal matah (raw shallot-chili-lime-lemongrass relish) on the side in a small saucer. A small portion of steamed white rice in a bowl. Served on a banana leaf, on a worn wooden warung table, a glass of iced tea and a clay pot softly out of focus behind. Soft natural Balinese daylight from the open shopfront, viewed from about 40 degrees above, 35mm lens, moderate depth of field. Everyday unstyled serving, slightly messy edges with char and oil, true-to-life colours, realistic textures. The meat must be wound in a continuous rope-spiral on the skewer, not in cubes, not in ribbons, not flat. No food styling, no microgreens, no fusion garnishes, no studio lighting, no text, no logos, no people, no hands.
